notes: Key finding: there is no full 2026 Canadian Drowning Report. The lifesaving.org link '2026 Canadian Drowning Report (English)' (file 361108) opens the same one-page National Drowning Data Snapshot already in the ledger (also at lifesaving.ca and lifesavingsociety.com); it prints percentages only and no counts per setting. The latest full multi-page national report is the 2025 Edition (data 2017–2021, 29 pages, file dated April 2026 on lifesaving.ca; same as lifesaving.org file 354621 '2025 Canadian Drowning Report - Extended'). Its page 18 body-of-water chart also prints percentages only (Lake/pond 36, River 27, Bathtub 14, Pool 9, Other 9, Ocean 5, Lifeguard-supervised 1); the only counts per setting are two printed five-year averages, 176 lake/pond deaths per year and 67 bathtub deaths per year. Those are returned as rows; status is partial because counts for the other settings and for 2018–2022 are not printed anywhere found. Verdict on the pairing: 15% belongs to Bathtubs and 7% to Other, not the reverse. Basis: (1) in the 2026 snapshot the tokens run '9% Pools <1% Drowning in a lifeguard supervised setting 7% Other 15% Bathtubs', and the only reading that gives every label one value is value-before-label; (2) the Alberta 2026 snapshot uses the identical template and extracts as '7% Pools and hot tubs <2% ... 8% Other 28% Bathtubs', while the Society's own news post states Alberta bathtub drownings rose to 28%, so the number immediately before 'Bathtubs' is the bathtub share; (3) the bathing activity share equals the bathtub location share in every edition checked (national 2026: 15 and 15; Alberta 2026: 28 and 28; national 2025 edition: 14 and 14). This has still not been seen on a rendered page; a person with a browser should open the snapshot PDF and look at the 'WHERE ARE THEY DROWNING?' graphic. 2022 flag: the snapshot's printed partial-data notes name 2016–2021 only ('The 2016–2021 totals are based on partial data'; 'Death rate and number of deaths per year for 2016–2021 are based on partial data'); 2022 is not flagged partial. The sentence 'Complete information for British Columbia was not available at the time of data collection' is the last sentence of the general introductory paragraph, directly after the 2016–2021 sentence; the 2025 Edition's page 6 footnote ties the partial data explicitly to missing British Columbia data for 2016–2021. So 2022 carries the general BC caveat but no explicit partial flag. Activity split, 2018–2022 (snapshot, label-then-value, unambiguous): Boating 22%, Bathing 15%, Aquatic 26%, Non-aquatic 17% (sum 80; remainder not printed). 2017–2021 (2025 Edition, p.21): Boating 23%, Aquatic 26%, Non-aquatic 18%, Land/ice/air travel 11% (sum 78); boating types: powerboat 57, canoe 18, kayak 8, inflatable craft 4, sailboat 2; purpose: recreational 55, daily living 29, unknown 11, occupational 3, attempting rescue 2 (average 10 rescue deaths per year); bathing is 48% of daily-living deaths. Revision: the 2025 Edition prints 2017–2021 as 465, 485, 428, 544, 502 (total 2,424, average 485 per year); the 2026 snapshot prints 465, 488, 430, 552, 509 and explains that additional Alberta cases from 2018 to 2021 were identified in 2026. Coincidental sums for the checker: 15 (bathing) + 7 (other) = 22 (boating) and 9 (pools) + 17 (non-aquatic) = 26 (aquatic) in 2018–2022, and 9 (pool) + 9 (other) = 18 (non-aquatic) in 2017–2021; these are different partitions and nothing was summed. Layout check by the lab session (21 Oct 2026): the snapshot PDF was opened in a browser and the text positions read; on page 1 the label Bathtubs sits at about x 289, y 702 with 15% at x 349, y 738 directly beside it, and the label Other at x 414, y 762 with 7% at x 420, y 727 directly above it, so 15% is Bathtubs and 7% is Other, as this bundle concluded. The same read gives Ocean 6% in the 2026 snapshot (the 2025 Edition prints 5%), Lakes 36%, Rivers 27%, Pools 9% and lifeguard-supervised under 1%.
